column1: # memfn/tests/g2_units.tsv -- the UNITS of run_g2.sh --quick (R-39) and their declared weights.
# A unit is a block of run_g2.sh that runs, judges and reports on its own: want UNIT / udone UNIT mark
# its edges there, and `g2_parts.py assign` deals the units to the N parts of `--part K/N` by a
# deterministic greedy rule over the weights below (heaviest first, to the lightest part so far; ties
# to the lower part number, then to the table order). NO run-time state enters the assignment.
# The generator stage (the prelude) is run by every part and is no unit.
# Columns (TAB-separated): unit, weight (seconds, a RELATIVE cost), weight_source.
# SCALE: seconds a unit takes ALONE on the Linux dev box at G2_JOBS=2, nice 10 (lane r39's slice runs, 2026-11-10/11, each
# `--units NAME`). Two units could not be run alone without being a full run's longest leg (gcc, simd): their weight is the
# 2026-11-03 CI log's seconds divided by 1.4, the CI/box ratio of the units both measured (win 59/53, any 36/23, k1 19/13).
# Re-weight from the `G2UNIT name seconds` lines of a split run (a part's units overlap in time, so these
# are wall seconds inside the part, not CPU): scripts of the gate job 591 print them. A weight is a
# balance input only; a wrong weight costs balance, never coverage (g2_parts.py gather proves coverage).
